[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided tips for improving Downward-Facing Dog pose, including:  
1. Start with a strong foundation (hands shoulder-width apart, fingers spread wide).  
2. Activate your core (engage abdominal muscles).  
3. Lengthen your spine (keep it long and straight).  
4. Hips and heels (move hips back and up, heels grounded).  
5. Engage your legs (draw knees towards your chest).  
6. Weight distribution (distribute weight evenly between hands and feet).  
7. Shoulder alignment (keep shoulders down and away from ears).  
8. Chest expansion (open and broaden the chest).  
9. Gaze (look down towards the ground).  
10. Breathing (take slow, deep breaths).  

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips for Downward-Facing Dog pose included using props, engaging glutes, and practicing variations.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested restorative yoga poses targeting hamstrings and calves, including:  
1. Legs Up The Wall Pose (Viparita Karani).  
2. Reclined Pigeon Pose (Supta Eka Pada Rajakapotasana).  
3. Reclined Hamstring Stretch (Supta Prasarita Padottanasana).  
4. Calves and Ankles Pose (Vrksasana Variation).  
5. Seated Forward Fold with Legs Straight (Paschimottanasana Variation).  

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant emphasized using props, breathing deeply, staying in poses for 5-10 minutes, and listening to the body
